summary: Cyprus naturalised 6,779 people by exception from July 2007 to August 2020 (Nikolatos inquiry), and the Audit Office counts 3,517 investors and 3,810 family members up to the last approvals in July 2021. The official record is unusually rich: a 786-page inquiry report with the criteria and naturalisation counts for each of 12 rule periods, three Audit Office reports, the 2020 regulations, and government statements on revocations (360 persons decided since 2021, 112 completed by Sept 2025) and the EU infringement case (closed March 2026). The weak spots are money (only a Ministry of Finance estimate of EUR 6.6bn of transactions 2013-2018, cited second-hand), nationality splits, and the investor permanent-residence scheme (Regulation 6(2)), for which we found the 2023 criteria but no official count of permits.

programs.name: Cyprus Investment Programme (Κυπριακό Επενδυτικό Πρόγραμμα, ΚΕΠ), incl. the 2007-2013 scheme for exceptional naturalisation of foreign investors
programs.notes: Naturalisation by Council of Ministers decision, without residence: 2007-2013 under para 2(στ) of the Third Schedule of the Civil Registry Law (exceptional services), from 30 Apr 2013 under art. 111A(2) (Law 36(I)/2013), from 18 Aug 2020 under regulations ΚΔΠ 379/2020. Criteria changed 12 times by Council decisions. Abolished by decision of 13 Oct 2020: no applications after 31 Oct 2020; pending ones approved until 31 Jul 2021. 6,779 naturalisations to 17 Aug 2020 (inquiry); 3,517 investors and 3,810 family members to 31 Jul 2021 (Audit Office). Art. 111A(2) deleted by a law passed in late 2025 or early 2026; EU infringement closed 11 Mar 2026.

programs.name: Cyprus fast-track permanent residence for investors (Άδεια Μετανάστευσης, Regulation 6(2) of the Aliens and Immigration Regulations; 'golden visa')
programs.notes: Permanent residence (Immigration Permit) for third-country investors, issued by the Minister of Interior under Regulation 6(2); EUR 300,000 investment plus EUR 50,000 annual income (2023 criteria). No right to work except as director of the invested company. Card valid 10 years; right of residence unlimited. It does not lead to citizenship by itself; naturalisation needs years of actual residence under the ordinary rules (not researched here). Launch date and pre-2021 terms not verified. No official numbers of permits found.

gaps: Regulation 6(2) investor permanent residence: no official count of permits granted, renewed or cancelled was found for any year. The Audit Office 'Golden Visa' report of 9 Nov 2023 probably has figures but could not be located (not on gov.cy/audit, no Wayback copy). Parliament (parliament.cy) answers could not be searched: the site blocks automated access.

Regulation 6(2) terms before 2021: the 1st-3rd revisions of the criteria (including the 24 Mar 2021 text) and the launch date of the fast-track policy were not found; only the 2023 Ministry announcement describes the previous EUR 300,000 rule.

CIP applications received, rejected and withdrawn per year for the whole programme: only the Audit Office chart of approved applications by filing year (2007-2020) and the 2018-2020 snapshot (1,597 filed after 21 May 2018) were found. No official total of applications received or rejected over 2007-2020.

Naturalisations by nationality: no official breakdown found (the inquiry report gives none in its text layer). Only Al Jazeera's leak-based counts (Russia 1,000, China 500, Ukraine 100 applicants among 2017-2019 approvals), not recorded as observations because they cover only the leaked files.

Money collected: no official totals of the EUR 75,000/100,000 donations to the Research and Innovation Foundation and the Land Development Corporation, of fees, or of investment per year. The only total is the Ministry of Finance study's EUR 6.6bn of transactions 2013-2018 as summarised by the inquiry; the study itself (Feb 2019, updated Sept 2020) was not found.

Revocations: the government's figures conflict over time (41 decisions/150 persons since March 2023 in Sept-Oct 2025 vs 39 decisions/147 persons in March 2026), and there is no complete official list by year. The Kalogirou committee report on revocations was not found.

Criminal case: the outcome of the Nicosia Assize Court judgment of 23 Jan 2025 (believed to be the case over Al Jazeera's undercover film) is not in the Law Office statement; the judgment was not found on CyLaw in this pass.
The 2025/2026 law deleting art. 111A(2): number and gazette date not found.
The Commission's own closure decision for INFR(2020)2276 (11 Mar 2026) was not found; only the Cypriot Law Office's announcement. The EC infringement database could not be queried (endpoint moved).

Audit Office 2022 report Annex 1 (the inquiry's description of the programme, PDF pp. 153-189) is scanned images without a text layer and was not OCR'd (no Greek language data available for tesseract).
